3	## Bootstrapping a manifest on an artifact that has none
4	
5	Most existing plans won't have a manifest yet — that's why features have been getting lost. To create one:
6	
7	1. Read the current version completely.
8	2. List every distinct feature, rule, section, behavior, constraint, special case, data field, and capability. Err toward over-listing; a manifest with too many items is safe, one with too few leaks.
9	3. Group related items so the list stays scannable (e.g. "Scoring", "UI tabs", "Data/export", "Special rules").
10	4. Present the list to the user: "Here's what I read as the locked features of the current version. Confirm or correct, and I'll pin this so nothing drops in future edits."
11	5. Once confirmed, embed it using the format below that matches the artifact.
12	
13	## Templates by format
14	
15	### Markdown / text doc
16	Pin at the very top:
17	
18	```markdown
19	<!-- FEATURE MANIFEST — v3 — confirmed 2026-05-28
20	Scoring: accuracy-based star ratings; tiered grade lock/mastery gate
21	Daily: date-seeded daily shuffle
22	Special: export only for admins
23	-->
24	```
25	
26	Or, if the user wants it human-visible, a collapsible section:
27	
28	```markdown
29	## 🔒 Locked Features (v3)
30	- Accuracy-based star ratings
31	- Tiered grade lock / mastery gate
32	- Date-seeded daily shuffle
33	```
34	
35	### App / code (single-file HTML, etc.)
36	Header comment at the top of the main file:
37	
38	```html
39	<!--
40	FEATURE MANIFEST v3
41	- Offline cache, sync on reconnect
42	- Weekly reset every Monday
43	- Parent PIN on settings
44	- Two-export workflow
45	-->
46	```
47	
48	Keep it updated in the same edit that changes behavior, so the manifest and the code never drift apart.
49	
50	### Spreadsheet
51	Either freeze rows 1–N as a manifest block above the data, or add a sheet named `_Manifest` with one feature per row and a "confirmed" date column. The frozen-row approach is more visible; the separate sheet keeps the data area clean.
52	
53	### Pasted-in-chat (no file)
54	No storage location exists, so:
55	- Restate the manifest as a short block at the top of every new version you output.
56	- Run the regression table in chat each turn.
57	- If the plan is getting large, suggest moving it to a file so the manifest can be pinned and the cost of restating drops.
58

60	
61	- Update it in the SAME edit that adds or removes a feature — never in a separate pass.
62	- When the user intentionally removes a feature, delete it from the manifest AND note the removal in that turn's regression table.
